$comment: A tenancy, chosen because its identity comes from a third place again.
The MSA's comes from commercial architecture, the employment contract's largely
from statute, and this one's partly from FORMALITY: a lease can say everything
correctly and still be legally ineffective because of something done, or not done,
outside the four corners of the document.

Two of these are not CONTENT requirements at all. A clause reading 'the parties shall register this Agreement' does not make the instrument registered, and reporting such a requirement RESOLVED because the clause is present would tell a user their lease is complete when section 49 of the Registration Act, 1908 bars it from being received in evidence. The best a document can achieve is PROVIDED_FOR.

requirements.identity_test: Remove it and there is no demise: section 105 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 requires a transfer of a right to enjoy identified immoveable property.

requirements.statement: The rent and the period of the tenancy are stated.
requirements.identity_test: Remove either and there is no lease under section 105, which requires a price paid or promised and a certain time, express or implied.

requirements.statement: Delivery of possession and its return are dealt with.
requirements.identity_test: Remove it and section 108(b) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 implies the obligation, but neither party has a stated date, condition or inventory to hold the other to.

requirements.statement: Any security deposit, and the terms on which it is returned, are stated.
requirements.identity_test: Remove it and the largest sum the tenant hands over is governed by nothing.

requirements.statement: Who bears utilities, taxes and maintenance is stated.
requirements.identity_test: Remove it and a running cost of the tenancy is allocated by implication, which is how a tenant comes to be told after the fact that the electricity was always theirs.
Remove it and section 108 supplies defaults that few landlords and no tenants have read.

requirements.statement: How the tenancy ends, and on what notice.
requirements.identity_test: Remove it and section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 supplies the notice period by implication from the purpose of the letting.

requirements.statement: The instrument bears the stamp duty the applicable State law requires.
requirements.identity_test: Remove it and section 35 of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 makes the document inadmissible in evidence for any purpose — the tenancy may be perfectly drafted and unenforceable in the only forum that matters.
requirements.outside_the_document: Stamping and registration are acts performed on the instrument, not statements made in it. The most a clause can do is provide for them.

requirements.statement: The instrument is registered where the law requires registration.
requirements.identity_test: Remove it and a lease from year to year, or for a term exceeding one year, is void as a lease under section 107 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, and section 49 of the Registration Act, 1908 bars it from being received as evidence of the transaction.
requirements.outside_the_document: Stamping and registration are acts performed on the instrument, not statements made in it. The most a clause can do is provide for them.
